en: The Mahāsukha-vajra-amogha-tattva-samaya-sūtra. [Translated by] Kai-fu-yi-tong-san-si,
Te-jin, Shi Hong-lu-qing, Duke of Su with a fief of three thousand households,
invested with purple robes, posthumously titled Sikong, posthumous title Dazheng, and honorific name Da.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Great Xingshan Temple, of Vast Wisdom, by Imperial Decree. The Chapter on the Essential Principles of the Prajñāpāramitā. Thus have I heard:

At one time the Bhagavat—having accomplished the samaya-wisdom of the vajra-consecration of all Tathāgatas of supreme excellence; having received the jeweled crown of consecration from all Tathāgatas and become the Lord of the Three Realms; having realized the omniscience of all Tathāgatas and attained mastery in yoga; capable of performing all various activities through the equality of all seals (mudrās) of all Tathāgatas; for the sake of the entire realm of sentient beings, inexhaustible and without remainder, having brought to complete fulfillment all their intentions and karmic activities; at all times throughout the three periods of the eternal past, present, and future—the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, whose body, speech, and mind are adamantine.

It was situated within the palace of the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven in the desire realm, a place where all Tathāgatas constantly dwell. It was a magnificent great maṇi hall, praised for its auspiciousness, adorned with various interspersed bells, silk banners, and tassels that were stirred by gentle breezes, and further embellished with pearl necklaces, jeweled garlands, and crescent and full-moon ornaments.
He was accompanied by a multitude of eighty koṭis of bodhisattvas, namely:

the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadyaścittotpādadharmacakrapravartin, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvamārapramardin.
Surrounded and venerated by such a multitude of great bodhisattvas, he preached the Dharma for them— a teaching excellent in the beginning,
middle, and end, with skillful phrasing and meaning, uniform, complete, pure, and immaculate, expounding the gateway of the pure phrases of all dharmas.
That is to say:
"The phrase 'wondrously attuned purity' is the stage of a bodhisattva;
the phrase 'purity of the arrow of desire' is the stage of a bodhisattva."
The phrase "purity of contact" is the stage of a bodhisattva;
the phrase "purity of the bonds of craving" is the stage of a bodhisattva;
the phrase "purity of the sovereign lord of all" is the stage of a bodhisattva.
The phrase "purity of vision" is the stage of a bodhisattva;
the phrase "purity of delight" is the stage of a bodhisattva;
the phrase "purity of affection" is the stage of a bodhisattva.
The phrase "purity of pride" is a stage of the bodhisattva;
the phrase "purity of adornment" is a stage of the bodhisattva;
the phrase "purity of the moistening of the mind" is a stage of the bodhisattva.
The phrase "purity of radiance" is the stage of a bodhisattva;
the phrase "purity of bodily bliss" is the stage of a bodhisattva;
the phrase "purity of form" is the stage of a bodhisattva.
The phrase "purity of sound" is the stage of a bodhisattva;
the phrase "purity of fragrance" is the stage of a bodhisattva;
the phrase "purity of taste" is the stage of a bodhisattva.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are pure by their very nature, the perfection of wisdom is pure, Vajrapāṇi!

If anyone hears this *prajñāpāramitā* principle of the birth of purity, until they reach the seat of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), all veils and obscurations—namely the afflictive obscurations, the cognitive obscurations, and the karmic obscurations—even if extensively accumulated, will certainly not cause them to fall into the realms such as the hells.
Even if one has committed grave offenses, it is not difficult to extinguish them.

If one can receive and uphold this [teaching], reciting and reading it daily while reflecting upon it with focused attention, one will, in this very life, realize the Vajra Samādhi of the Equality of All Dharmas. One will attain mastery over all dharmas, experience immeasurable joy and bliss, and through the birth as one of the sixteen great Bodhisattvas, obtain the rank of Tathāgata and Vajradhara.

At that time, the Bhagavān—the supreme *vajrasattva* who holds the *vajra* of all maṇḍalas of the *samaya* of the Mahāyāna realization of all Tathāgatas; he who has subdued all within the three realms without exception; the one who accomplishes all aims; the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi—in order to clarify this meaning, smiled radiantly and with joy. With his left hand he formed the *vajra-māna-mudrā*, and with his right hand he brandished the primordial Great *Vajra*, assuming a posture of heroic valor.

He then uttered the heart-mantra of the *Mahāsukha-vajra-amogha-samaya*: “HŪṂ. Then the Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata further proclaimed this *prajñāpāramitā-naya* of the manifest awakening to the peaceful *dharmatā* of all Tathāgatas.
That is to say:
"The manifest perfect awakening to the equality of the vajra, because great bodhi is as firm as a vajra;
the manifest perfect awakening to the equality of meaning, because great bodhi has the single purpose of benefit."
One realizes perfect awakening to the equality of phenomena, because the intrinsic nature of great enlightenment is pure;
one realizes perfect awakening to the equality of all karma, because the nature of great enlightenment is free from all conceptualization and non-conceptualization.

Vajrapāṇi! If there be anyone who hears these four methods of origination, reads, recites, accepts, and upholds them, even if they have currently committed immeasurable grave offenses, they will certainly be able to transcend all evil destinies, and shall eventually sit at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), swiftly attaining supreme perfect awakening.

When the Bhagavān had thus spoken, desiring to further clarify this meaning, he smiled radiantly, assumed the *jñānamuṣṭi-mudrā* (the seal of the wisdom-fist), and uttered the Heart-Mantra of the Equal Nature of All Dharmas:
*Āḥ Hūṃ*. Then, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, who subdues those difficult to tame, further proclaimed the *Prajñāpāramitā-naya*, the most supreme source of the equality of all dharmas.
That is to say:
because desire has the nature of being without conceptual proliferation, hatred has the nature of being without conceptual proliferation;
because hatred has the nature of being without conceptual proliferation, delusion has the nature of being without conceptual proliferation.
Because ignorance has the nature of being free from conceptual proliferation (*aprapañca*), all phenomena have the nature of being free from conceptual proliferation;
because all phenomena have the nature of being free from conceptual proliferation, one should know that the *prajñāpāramitā* has the nature of being free from conceptual proliferation.

Vajrapāṇi! If anyone hears this principle, receives and upholds it, reads and recites it—even if they were to harm all sentient beings within the three realms—they shall not fall into the evil destinies; rather, for the sake of subduing them, they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Then, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, wishing to further clarify this meaning, assumed the seal of Trailokyavijaya; with a lotus-like face, smiling yet with a wrathful frown and a fierce gaze, his sharp fangs bared, he stood in the posture of subjugation and uttered this heart-mantra of the Vajra-hūṃkāra:

"HŪṂ" (short). At that time, the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata of the Dharmatā of Innate Purity, further proclaimed the Principle of Prajñā arising from the Wisdom-Seal of the Universal Equality of All Phenomena, Avalokiteśvara.
That is to say:
"Because all worldly desires are pure, all hatred is pure;
because all worldly defilements are pure, all transgressions are pure."
Because all phenomena in the world are pure, all sentient beings are pure;
because all-knowledge of the world is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure.

Vajrapāṇi! If there be anyone who hears this principle, upholds it, recites it, and contemplates it with focused attention, even if they dwell amidst the various desires, they will remain like a lotus flower, unstained by adventitious defilements, and shall swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, wishing to further clarify this meaning, smiled with a joyful countenance, assumed the posture of an opening lotus flower, and—observing desire without being stained by it—spoke of the various forms and minds of all sentient beings:
"Hrīḥ. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Lord of the Entire Triple World, further proclaimed the *Prajñā-naya*, the Treasury of Wisdom for the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas.
That is to say:
"By the gift of consecration, one is able to attain the rank of Dharma King over the three realms;
by the gift of meaningful benefit, all wishes and aspirations are fulfilled."
"By means of the gift of Dharma, one attains the perfection of all dharmas;
by means of the gift of material necessities, one attains all peace and happiness of body, speech, and mind.

At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, wishing to further clarify this meaning, smiled with a joyful countenance, bound a vajra-jewel garland upon his own head, and spoke the heart-mantra of the Jewel of All Empowerment Samaya:
“Tāṃ. Then the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata who has attained the Wisdom-Seal of all Tathāgatas, further proclaimed the Prajñāpāramitā-naya of the empowerment of the Wisdom-Seals of all Tathāgatas.
That is to say:
"By holding the body-seal (*kāyamudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, one becomes the body of all Tathāgatas;
by holding the speech-seal (*vāṅmudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, one attains the Dharma of all Tathāgatas."
By holding the heart-seal (*hṛdaya-mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, one immediately realizes the samādhi of all Tathāgatas;
by holding the vajra-seal (*vajra-mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, one accomplishes the supreme siddhi of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

Vajrapāṇi! If there be anyone who hears this principle, upholds it, recites it, contemplates it with focused attention, they shall attain all sovereignty, the wisdom of omniscience, all activities, and all accomplishments; they shall attain the vajra-nature of all body, speech, and mind, and all siddhis, and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Then the Bhagavān, wishing to clarify this meaning, smiled radiantly and, forming the Great Samaya Seal of the Vajra Fist, spoke this Heart Mantra of the Samaya of the Siddhi of All Firm Vajra Seals: "Aḥ.
Then the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata Free from All Conceptual Elaborations, further spoke the Prajñāpāramitā Principle of the Revolving Wheel of Syllables.
That is to say:
"All phenomena are empty, because they are in accord with the absence of intrinsic nature;
all phenomena are signless, because they are in accord with the signless nature."
"All phenomena are wishless, because they are conjoined with the nature of wishlessness;
all phenomena are luminous, because the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure.

Then, the youth Mañjuśrī, wishing to further clarify this meaning, smiled radiantly and, brandishing his own sword, struck all the Tathāgatas and spoke this most supreme heart-mantra of the *prajñāpāramitā*:
At that time, the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata Sarvatathāgatamahācakra-praviṣṭa, further proclaimed the Prajñāpāramitā-naya of Entering the Great Wheel. It is said:
"By entering the equality of the Vajra, one enters the Dharma-wheel of all Tathāgatas."
Entering into the equality of meanings is to enter the wheel of the great bodhisattvas;
entering into the equality of all phenomena is to enter the wheel of the sublime Dharma;
entering into the equality of all karmas is to enter the wheel of all activities.

Then, at that moment, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Citta-utpāda-cakra-pravartana, wishing to further clarify this meaning, smiled with a joyful countenance, turned the vajra-wheel, and uttered the heart-mantra of all vajra-samayas:
“HŪṂ. Thereupon, the Bhagavān Tathāgata Viśva-tathāgata-pūjā-garbha-vistara-vidhi, further proclaimed the Prajñā-naya of the Supreme Origination of All Offerings.
That is to say:
"To give rise to the bodhicitta is to perform a vast offering to all Tathāgatas;
to rescue and deliver all sentient beings is to perform a vast offering to all Tathāgatas."
To uphold the sublime scriptures is to perform a vast offering to all Tathāgatas;

to uphold, read, recite, write oneself or instruct others to write, contemplate, and cultivate the Prajñāpāramitā, and to offer various kinds of worship to it, is to perform a vast offering to all Tathāgatas.
Then, the Great Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, wishing to further clarify this meaning, smiled with a joyful countenance and spoke this *sarvakarmāśūnyatāsamaya-sarvavajrahṛdaya*: "Oṃ.
At that time, the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Śāstṛdhṛtajñānamuṣṭi, further proclaimed the *prajñāpāramitānaya* of the treasury of wisdom for the subjugation of all beings.
That is to say:
"Because all sentient beings are equal, wrath is equal;
because all sentient beings are to be tamed, wrath is to be tamed."
Because all sentient beings have the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), they have the nature of wrath;
because all sentient beings have the nature of the vajra, they have the nature of the wrathful vajra. Why is this?
"The subduing of all sentient beings is itself enlightenment.

At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin, wishing to further clarify this meaning, smiled radiantly and, assuming the form of a Vajrayakṣa while brandishing vajra-fangs, struck terror into all the Tathāgatas. He then uttered the heart-mantra of the Great Laughter of Vajra Wrath:
"HAḤ. Thereupon, the Bhagavān Sarvasamatāvyavasthita-tathāgata further proclaimed the Prajñāpāramitā-naya of the Supreme Arising of the Samaya of All Dharmas.
That is to say:
"Because all things are equal in nature, the perfection of wisdom is equal in nature;
because all things are beneficial in nature, the perfection of wisdom is beneficial in nature."
Because it is the nature of all phenomena, the *prajñāpāramitā* is the nature of phenomena;
because it is the nature of all activities, it should be understood that the *prajñāpāramitā* is the nature of activities.
Then Vajrapāṇi entered the samādhi of the empowerment of the *samaya* of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas, and uttered the heart-mantra of the All-Accomplishing *Samaya*:
"HŪṂ. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, further proclaimed the principle of the Prajñā empowerment for all sentient beings.
That is to say:
"All sentient beings are the Tathāgatagarbha, because they possess the universal self of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
all sentient beings are the Vajragarbha, because they have received the empowerment of the Vajragarbha."
It is the treasury of the sublime Dharma for all sentient beings, because it can transform all languages;
it is the treasury of karma for all sentient beings, because it accords with the nature of that which acts and that which is acted upon.
At that time, the Outer Vajra Family, wishing to further clarify this meaning, made a sound of joy and spoke the self-realization-heart-mantra of Vajreśvara:
*tad* (two syllables). Then, the various Mātṛkā goddesses prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and offered their own samaya-realization-heart-mantras for summoning, entering, slaying, and accomplishing:
*viyu* (two syllables). At that time, the three brothers of the Mṛtyu-kāla deities and others personally prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and offered their own heart-mantras.
*Svāhā*. At that time, the four sister goddesses offered their own hearts: *Khaṃ*.

Then the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata of Infinite and Boundless Ultimate Realization, in order to empower this teaching and bring it to ultimate perfection, further proclaimed the Prajñāpāramitā-naya of the Arising of the Equal Vajra.
That is to say:
"Because the *prajñāpāramitā* is immeasurable, all Tathāgatas are immeasurable;
because the *prajñāpāramitā* is boundless, all Tathāgatas are boundless."
Because all phenomena are of one nature, the perfection of wisdom is of one nature;
because all phenomena are ultimate, the perfection of wisdom is ultimate.
Vajrapāṇi! If there be anyone who hears this principle, upholds, recites, and contemplates its meaning, they shall attain the ultimate perfection of all the practices of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

Then the Bhagavān Vairocana, the Tathāgata who has attained the non-conceptual nature of all secret dharmas, further expounded the Prajñāpāramitā-naya of the Vajradharmatā—the Unfailing Samaya-Vajra of Great Bliss, which is supreme and devoid of beginning, middle, or end.
That is to say:
"Because the bodhisattva-mahāsattva achieves the supreme fulfillment of great desire, they attain the supreme fulfillment of great bliss;
because the bodhisattva-mahāsattva achieves the supreme fulfillment of great bliss, they then attain the supreme fulfillment of the great bodhi of all Tathāgatas."
Because Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas attain the supreme accomplishment of the Great Bodhi of all Tathāgatas, they attain the supreme accomplishment of all Tathāgatas in crushing the great Māras;
because Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas attain the supreme accomplishment of all Tathāgatas in crushing the great Māras, they attain the accomplishment of being the sovereign lords of the three realms;

because Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas attain the accomplishment of being the sovereign lords of the three realms, they attain the supreme and ultimate accomplishment of purifying the dwelling, attachment, and cyclic existence of all sentient beings in the realm without remainder, constantly remaining in birth and death through great diligence to rescue, gather, benefit, and bring peace and happiness to all.
Why is this? "The Bodhisattva of supreme wisdom, until the very end of birth and death,
constantly acts for the benefit of sentient beings, yet does not proceed toward nirvana."
Through Prajñā and skillful means, sustained by the perfection of wisdom,
all phenomena and all modes of existence are entirely purified.
To tame the world through desire and the like, and to bring about their complete purification— this is the purpose.
Whether in the Peak of Existence or the miserable realms, they tame beings and exhaust all states of existence.
Like a lotus whose essence is inherently pure and unsullied by impurities, so too is the nature of all desires;
they remain untainted while benefiting all sentient beings.
One who desires great purity, great bliss and abundance,
and mastery over the three realms, is able to accomplish steadfast benefit. "Vajrapāṇi!..."

If there are those who hear this primordial *prajñāpāramitā-naya* and recite or listen to it every morning, they shall attain the ultimate *siddhi* of the Vajra-Āmoghasamaya, which is all-pervasive peace, joy, and great bliss. In this present life, they shall obtain mastery over all dharmas and the joy thereof, and through the manifestation of the sixteen Great Bodhisattvas, they shall attain the rank of a Tathāgata-Vajradhara.
"HŪṂ. At that time, all the Tathāgatas, as well as the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas such as Vajradhara and others, all gathered together.
Desiring to cause this Dharma to be unfailing, unimpeded, and swiftly accomplished, they all joined in praising Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
Mahāsattva! Excellent, excellent! Great Bliss!
Excellent, excellent! Mahāyāna! Excellent, excellent!
O Great Wisdom!
You are well able to expound this Dharma teaching; empowered by the Vajra Sūtra, whoever upholds this most supreme King of Teachings cannot be destroyed by any māras.
One shall attain the most supreme state of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and before long, achieve all *siddhis*.
After all the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas had together delivered this sublime teaching, they all rejoiced greatly and,
with faith and acceptance, put it into practice, so that the holders [of this mantra] might swiftly attain accomplishment.

en: The Treatise on the Mudrā of the Sovereign Vajramuṣṭi from the Mahāsukha-vajra-amogha-tattva-samaya-sūtra.
